definition: A theoretical distribution is a mathematically specified pattern of values that researchers try to fit to observed data so they can describe the data’s statistical properties and make further analyses possible. In the source, distributions such as the normal inverse Gaussian and generalized hyperbolic are treated as theoretical distributions used to model return data.

reasons: The packet supports a specific applied use of a theoretical distribution for bitcoin return data, but it does not define the term generally as a mathematically specified pattern of values.
The claims that researchers use it to describe data’s statistical properties and to make further analyses possible go beyond what the source states.
The source mentions the NIG and GH distributions in this one context; it does not establish the broader generalization implied by the definition.

The definition’s general description (“a mathematically specified pattern of values… researchers try to fit… so they can describe statistical properties and make further analyses possible”) is not fully supported by the packet; the packet states that a distribution is used to “fit the returns” and that this helps study “statistical properties,” but it does not explicitly support the full generic formulation or the claim about enabling “further analyses possible.”

The packet supports NIG being fitted to bitcoin return data (“The paper develops the ability of the normal inverse Gaussian distribution (NIG) to fit the returns of bitcoin”), but it does not clearly support the claim that generalized hyperbolic (GH) is “treated as [a] theoretical distribution … used to model return data”; it only says NIG’s out-of-sample adjustment is “similar to that of a generalized hyperbolic (GH) distribution,” without stating GH is used in the same way or is explicitly characterized as a theoretical distribution in the requested sense.

The definition asserts that the cited distributions are “treated as theoretical distributions”; while the packet uses the phrase “adjusting a theoretical distribution,” it does not explicitly define which distributions (NIG and GH) are being treated as “theoretical distributions” in the dictionary-like sense described.
